title: Containers: an app packed with its dependencies

kcs.statement: A container packages an application with its libraries and dependencies into an image that runs the same way on any host with a container runtime such as Docker.
Containers share the host's operating system kernel, so they start in seconds and pack more densely than virtual machines, each of which runs its own full guest operating system.

problem_ideas: A team says the app 'works on my laptop but not in production': explain how a container image prevents this.
Compare boot time and per-host density for 20 small services run as containers versus as separate EC2 instances.
Decide whether each item lives inside a container image: app code, language runtime, host kernel, system libraries.
Explain the difference between an AMI and a container image in one sentence each.
A monolith is being split into 12 microservices: why are containers a natural fit?
Spot the false statement: 'Each container runs its own full operating system kernel.'
